title: Windows 11 Gains Cloud Rebuild: Reinstall From the Cloud Even When the PC Won't Boot
excerpt: The KB5127936 preview update downloads a Windows image and your drivers from Windows Update — no USB stick needed — but it wipes the system disk, so read the warning first.
body:
• Microsoft's October 28 preview update KB5127936 adds Cloud rebuild, a recovery option that reinstalls Windows 11 using an image and drivers downloaded from Windows Update — including when the PC cannot start.
  • It is available as an optional update for Windows 11 versions 25H2 and 26H2 (builds 26200.9818 and 26300.9818), and it is rolling out gradually, so installing the update does not guarantee the option appears immediately.
  • Read the warning before you use it: Cloud rebuild reformats the system disk and removes all locally stored files, accounts, apps and settings. There is no keep-my-files option.
  • You need a working internet connection in the recovery environment, a healthy Windows Recovery Environment, and the PC plugged into power.

Every Windows user knows the dead-PC ritual: find another computer, download an installer, make a bootable USB stick, and hope the drivers work afterwards. Microsoft is trying to retire it. The October 28 preview update KB5127936 introduces Cloud rebuild, which, in Microsoft's own words, is "a new recovery option that reinstalls Windows 11 using a Windows image and device drivers downloaded from Windows Update, including when Windows is unable to start. No USB media or custom image is required."

How it works

"One known issue to note: some USB Audio Class 1.0 devices may show a "This device cannot start (Code 10)" error after recent updates."

If your PC still boots, you start from Settings > System > Recovery, choose Rebuild PC, and the machine restarts into the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) and begins the rebuild. If Windows will not boot at all, the PC drops into WinRE automatically after repeated failed starts; from there it is Troubleshoot > Recovery and uninstall > Cloud rebuild. You connect to wired Ethernet or Wi-Fi, review the target Windows build, edition and language, confirm the data-loss warning, and pick a file-removal option.

https://x.com/VideoCardz/status/2116938443288657991

The detail that separates Cloud rebuild from the existing Reset this PC cloud download is the drivers: the rebuild pulls device drivers from Windows Update along with the Windows image, so the machine comes back fully functional rather than missing its network or graphics drivers, as LockerGnome's walkthrough of Microsoft's documentation notes. WinRE in this update can also reuse eligible Wi-Fi profiles saved in Windows, so the recovery environment can get online on networks it already knows.

The part to read twice

Cloud rebuild is a clean install, not a repair install. Microsoft's documentation states that it reformats the system disk and removes all locally stored files, accounts, apps and settings; the PC returns to the out-of-box experience, like a new machine. Files in OneDrive or other cloud storage are unaffected, but anything stored only on the PC is gone. There are two erase choices: "Remove files," which is faster but leaves files potentially recoverable with specialist tools, and "Remove & sanitize files," which uses the storage hardware's own erase capability and is irreversible — the one to choose when a PC is being sold or handed on.

Requirements and rollout

The rebuild needs a healthy WinRE (you can check with reagentc /info in an elevated Command Prompt), a manufacturer-supplied networking driver inside WinRE, a PC that meets Windows 11's minimum hardware requirements, and a power cable — interrupting a rebuild can leave Windows unable to boot. Microsoft lists error codes for the common failures: 0x800704C6 means no network, 0xc1900200 means the PC fails the minimum requirements (most often TPM turned off), and 0xc1900224 means a needed networking or storage driver is missing from Windows Update. IT administrators can also configure and start a Cloud rebuild remotely through the Recovery CSP, using the installed build or a specified target build.

KB5127936 is an optional preview update for Windows 11 versions 25H2 and 26H2, found under Settings > Windows Update > Advanced options > Optional updates. Microsoft is rolling the feature out gradually, so it will reach devices in phases. The same update also adds a customisable File Explorer right-click menu and changes hibernation behaviour on Modern Standby laptops — less hibernation while the battery is above 80%, sooner hibernation below 10%. One known issue to note: some USB Audio Class 1.0 devices may show a "This device cannot start (Code 10)" error after recent updates.

steps.step: Install the optional KB5127936 preview update
steps.detail: Settings > Windows Update > Advanced options > Optional updates. The feature rolls out gradually, so it may not appear immediately.

steps.step: Back up anything stored only on the PC
steps.detail: Cloud rebuild reformats the system disk and removes all local files, accounts, apps and settings. Cloud-stored files are unaffected.
If the PC boots: Settings > System > Recovery > Rebuild PC. If it does not: in WinRE, choose Troubleshoot > Recovery and uninstall > Cloud rebuild.
Join Ethernet or Wi-Fi, review the target build, edition and language, and confirm the data-loss warning. Keep the PC plugged in.
"Remove files" is faster; "Remove & sanitize files" is irreversible and is the right choice before selling or handing on the PC.
